item.description: ORCHARD PARK - Monday night when the Buffalo Bills take on the Minnesota Vikings , Josh Allen will be back at the place where his legend first began taking shape. Buffalo’s only previous visit to U.S. Bank Stadium came in Week 3 of the 2018 season, and for Allen it was just his second NFL start. The odds were stacked against him and the Bills, literally, as the wise guys in Las Vegas installed the Bills as 17-point underdogs. But the newbie quarterback stunned NFL nation and during the Bills’ 27-6 blowout victory , he authored the first of probably about 100 meme-worthy plays, his never-to-be-forgotten leap over Vikings linebacker Anthony Barr . From that moment on he’s been a nonstop highlight reel. As is typically his way, he didn’t have much to say about the play because, as we’ve learned, Allen is very much a live-in-the-moment kind of guy, not one to dwell on past performances. “Honestly, not really,” he said when he was asked if it had crossed his mind that he’s returning to the scene of that first big play. But he did eventually elaborate when he was asked again about whether he was surprised by the crazy reaction that play got on social media with all the memes and later the t-shirts that were emblazoned with the picture of him leaping over Barr. "Surprised me, too," he said. "I was a good athlete in college. High school I was not. So as I got older and started to lift more weights, I guess I got a little more athletic. But yeah, I think it was just kind of a surprising thing for me too of what I was able to do, especially early on in the career with the running stuff. I know I still run a little bit now, but that was I think the moment that I was like, 'You know what? I do belong here.'" He then immediately spun forward and talked about how playing there will be nice in that there won’t be any weather to worry about, though it will be a difficult environment because of the Vikings’ passionate supporters who make that dome among the loudest venues in the NFL. “They're going to be a loud fan base,” he said. “Them being what their record is and kind of rolling right now, and their defense is playing outstanding football, so we're expecting an extremely loud crowd. That's a really, really good crowd. That's what I do remember about being there, early in that game just how loud it was, and they've got their Skol chant, which is an awesome tradition. It's going to be a fun experience.” Watch Bills vs Vikings on Fubo Buffalo Bills vs Minnesota Vikings game Date: Monday Start time: 8:15 p.m. Venue : U.S. Bank Stadium What channel is the Bills vs Vikings game? item.title: The missing piece that Roberto De Zerbi must slot into place after Tottenham's puzzling start
item.description: Tottenham arrived at Elland Road with three consecutive wins and departed disappointed by their failings in three departments. “We did not show character, we did not show personality, we did not show courage,” lamented Roberto De Zerbi and, if he was discussing the second half at Leeds, they amounted to fundamental failings for him. The temptation is to take a swipe at the forward line and say they were found wanting in three other areas: left winger, right winger and centre-forward. That is probably unfair on Mohammed Kudus , a considerable talent only a few starts into a comeback, and cruel to Mathys Tel , taken off before half-time with what De Zerbi fears is a bad injury. Spurs can argue that picking on those charged with scoring is harsh, given that they had seven goals from their three previous games before a powderpuff attack barely threatened Leeds. But the facts show that only Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Sunderland have scored fewer in the Premier League - and that may change after Sunday’s games. Only three of Spurs’ 10 have come from forwards: Dominic Solanke ’s injury-time equaliser at Old Trafford, Omar Marmoush’s thunderbolt against Coventry and Tel’s glorious solo goal at Chelsea. A case of quality rather than quantity, perhaps, even if they could all be damned by comparisons with the Ballon d’Or winner who used to deliver both for Spurs; that said, Harry Kane is on a four-game goal drought for Bayern Munich. It may be one of the few ways that Marmoush, whose own drought spans a mere three matches, ranks better than Kane. Yet the Egyptian is the face of a conundrum Spurs have created with their record outlay; while those three victories offered encouraging evidence that De Zerbi’s buys are having an impact in defence and midfield, the attacking acquisitions were Marmoush and Savio, who have a combined tally of one goal and no assists in the top flight. The Brazilian has not played for four weeks but, between them, they will earn Manchester City £145m. City seem to have got much the better of those deals. Savio has always faced the question of whether he can be productive enough and if he is best suited to the left or the right, Kudus’ best position. Marmoush increasingly faces the question of what he is: neither really a striker nor a winger. The Egyptian was prolific for Eintracht Frankfurt in a strike duo, alongside Hugo Ekitike; but De Zerbi does not play two up front. Solanke, more of a conventional spearhead, has four goals in his last 25 league games. item.title: Football match remembers WW1 Christmas truce
item.description: It was the first time Emmendingen FC had come to Newark to play [BBC] A football match commemorating the World War One Christmas truce has taken place in Nottinghamshire. On Christmas Day 1914, British and German troops stopped fighting and met at several locations in Belgium. A soldier from Newark, William Setchfield, was present at one near the village of Messines and he may have provided the football used during the truce. On Saturday, Newark Town played a side from its twin town of Emmendingen in what was billed a Peace Match. Luke Parsons, manager of Newark Town FC, said: "We've played previously. It's two histories, two cultures coming together to symbolise the friendship of what we are about." He added: "Obviously that was put down 108 years ago and we want to continue that with this game." The two teams have played each other twice before at the site of the front lines in Belgium for the centenary of the event. However, this was the first time Emmendingen FC had come to Newark to play. Parsons said: "It makes me incredibly proud to invite them over to England to fulfill another fixture." A replica World War One era football was exchanged between the teams [BBC] Jakob Griessbaum, captain of Emmendingen FC, said the team was "honoured" to visit and play in the match. "It's a nice opportunity for us to get together," he added. "We are happy to play football, to think about World War One and what happened there." Francis Towndrow, local historian for Newark Town FC, who was at the game, said the score in the two previous encounters was 4-1 to the German team, and then 2-2, but Newark won on penalties. "The Germans have been itching to play again to beat us so it's wonderful they are here," he added. The final score of the game, played at the YMCA centre in Lord Hawke Way on Saturday, was a 2-0 win to Newark. The Blues thanked Emmendingen and wished them "safe travels home", adding: "Thank you to all that came out to support. "Football is the winner. Fantastic to be a part of." The Peace Match kicked off at 14:00 GMT at the YMCA centre in Lord Hawke Way [BBC] Towndrow said research had revealed accounts of how good Setchfield was as a goalkeeper. He added: "We can from that deduce that he may have played in goal that day and also that [the] football he got for Christmas was used." Towndrow said Setchfield survived the war and stayed in the Nottinghamshire area. He died in 1959 at the age of 71. item.description: Elversberg take record-breaking crowd to Borussia Dortmund Elversberg took 8,000 fans to the Signal Iduna Park for their Bundesliga clash against Borussia Dortmund. Although suffering a 2-1 defeat, their fourth in 2026/27, memories will have been created to last a lifetime for generations of Elversberg’s travelling contingent. But what makes the figure more impressive, is that it’s a club record for Elversberg, who had never played higher than Germany’s 3. Liga until 2023. Additionally, the 8,000 travelling supporters makes up 61 percent of the town’s population – it really is that small! Speaking prior to Elversberg’s trip to Elversberg, head coach Vincent Wagner said: “Hooray, the whole community is here.” And despite being 2-0 down thanks to Felix Nmecha’s second-half brace , Noel Futkeu’s 81st-minute bicycle kick almost kickstarted a comeback. Defeat at the Signal Iduna Park leaves the Saarland club on 13 points from a possible 27 after nine matchdays, a commendable tally for a club that was playing in Germany’s fourth tier in 2022. item.title: Cincinnati provides update on JV Gibson injury
item.description: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 07: Cincinnati Bearcats receiver JV Gibson tries to break free of a Houston Cougars defender during the second quarter of a college football game between the Cincinnati Bearcats and Houston Cougars on Saturday, November 07, 2026 at TDECU Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by Austin McAfee/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With roughly seven minutes remaining in a heated Big 12 showdown between Cincinnati and Houston, the atmopshere inside TDECU Stadium abruptly changed. The crowd fell silent, and the passion and energy inside the building quickly turned into concern. Cincinnati wide receiver JV Gibson suffered a frightening collision with Houston strong safety Jordan Allen while running a post route toward the end zone. The impact left Cincinnati’s leading receiver motionless on the field, prompting officials to throw flags for pass interference and targeting penalties. But the officiating decisions quickly became secondary. As Gibson remained down with an apparent head injury, medical personnel rushed onto the field to attend the receiver. Members of the Cincinnati roster left the sideline to gathered around their teammate, kneeling nearby as trainers continued their evaluations. Gibson’s parents eventually made their way to the field as well. The game was delayed 16 minutes as medical personnel stabilized Gibson, placed him on a stretcher, and transported out of TDECU Stadium. His father accompanied him on the back of the medical cart. Gibson subsequently made his way to Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center. Before his departure, Cincinnati Athletics reported the receiver as “alert and moving all extremities.” “Our personnel did an amazing job to get out there very quickly, they were right on top of JV,” Cincinnati head coach Scott Satterfield said in the immediate aftermath of the game. “Ultimately, they got him in a good place there. He was moving all four extremities on command. They took him to the hospital for precautionary reasons, and obviously they got to do their CT scans and those type of things. I don’t have an update, but hopefully everything checks out great. I thought JV was playing awesome tonight and unfortunately that happened to him. Prayers go out to JV and his family, but it’s a blessing for him to move all four extremities. It’s always very scary, and scary for our team.” In a later update, Cincinnati’s official Twitter account confirmed that Gibson had been discharged from Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center and traveled back to Cincinnati with the team.

item.title: Real Madrid rediscover collective identity under Mourinho with eight consecutive victories
item.description: Real Madrid rediscover collective identity under Mourinho with eight consecutive victories Real Madrid have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past month, and the results have been there for everyone to see. Los Blancos secured a 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla last night to make it eight wins in their last eight games. Jose Mourinho’s tactical modifications have worked wonders for the Spanish club, and the performances have also improved. According to MARCA , he has moulded the team into a more cohesive and disciplined unit after a difficult start to his second spell in the Spanish capital. Mourinho’s Real Madrid growing stronger collectively Madrid have scored 24 goals across those eight matches, averaging three per game, while keeping three clean sheets. The winning run includes victories over Barcelona in El Clasico and Roma, RB Leipzig and AEK Athens in the Champions League. Saturday’s 3-0 victory over Valencia offered another example of their progress, with the team breaking down a resolute defensive unit. Jose Mourinho has galvanized the team at Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Los Che actually started the game very well, causing problems for Madrid, but goals from Fede Valverde, Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappe helped Mourinho’s men secure the three points. The most encouraging aspect of Real Madrid’s evolution is that the team no longer seem excessively dependent on individual brilliance. Mbappe, Guler, Diomande and Bellingham have come together to form an excellent attacking quartet, and their strengths complement each other perfectly. Mourinho’s defensive demands making the difference There was one moment in the Valencia game that perfectly summed up the defensive transformation under Mourinho. When Guler was caught out of position after Madrid lost possession, Mbappe sprinted across to cover the exposed space and restore the team’s defensive shape. One of the biggest criticisms levelled at the Frenchman was that he was not contributing enough defensively. How will Mourinho integrate Vinicius into the team? (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) That has changed now, with everyone willing to put the team ahead of themselves. Mourinho will love the fact that his side have almost reached that stage. It remains to be seen how the dynamics change once Vinicius Jr. returns from suspension and how the manager reintegrates him. If the team can find a way for Vinicius to thrive within this system too, they could become even more devastating in the coming months. It remains to be seen how Mourinho handles his return.

item.title: Barcelona new signing has a point to prove against Atletico Madrid after poor precedent
item.description: Barcelona new signing has a point to prove against Atletico Madrid after poor precedent Barcelona travel to the Metropolitano this weekend for one of the most important matches of the season. It promises to be an important game for many of the Barcelona players, including the new signing Anthony Gordon, who will play his first competitive game at the Metropolitano. Barcelona’s poor record against Atleti last season has already been well-documented , but this particular game is even more important for Gordon, who has had a bad precedent as well. The poor precedent Can Gordon make an impact against Atletico Madrid? (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As reported by Diario SPORT , Gordon has faced Atletico Madrid only once in his career. It was in August last year in the Sepa Cup, and it wasn’t the best of experiences for the winger. Deployed through the middle as Newcastle United slipped to a 2-0 defeat, it was a bruising afternoon for Gordon. The Englishman found fierce resistance from the Atleti defence and was eventually forced off in the 85th minute due to ankle discomfort. This could be an early reminder that Diego Simeone’s men could employ the same method when it comes to putting a halt to Gordon in the final third. This time, however, the Barcelona player will operate from the flanks, which should give the Englishman a higher degree of freedom. Pressure slowly growing Godon needs to up his performances once again. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) With three goals and five assists in all competitions, it will be perhaps unfair to criticise Gordon’s performances since joining Barcelona in the summer. The winger has won his battle with Karim Adeyemi for the left wing role, and established himself as a first-team regular. Yet, question marks remain. Gordon notably endured a poor outing against Real Madrid in the season’s first El Clasico and is still yet to score his first away goal in La Liga. His only goals in La Liga so far have come at home against Getafe and Alaves. That is quite a modest tally for a player of his quality. A strong performance against Atletico Madrid, to that end, could serve as an ideal confidence-booster for the former Newcastle United starlet, as he looks to solidify his role in Flick’s setup.

Every IPL trade update ahead of the 2027 mini-auction Franchises across the Indian Premier League are inching closer to finalising their retention lists for the 2027 season, with the mini-auction scheduled for December. Before that auction window opens, several teams are expected to explore trade routes first, swapping players outright or settling deals purely in cash, as a quicker way to patch up squad gaps before bidding even begins. Over the years, several marquee names, including Hardik Pandya, Robin Uthappa and Cameron Green, have switched franchises through trade deals rather than the auction table. Another bowler-friendly track at Seddon Park is a real possibility, but the final answer may depend as much on the clouds over Hamilton as on the strip itself. The third ODI between New Zealand and India is scheduled for Tuesday, 10 November, with the first ball due at 3:00 PM local time (NZDT), which is 7:30 AM in India. India lead the five-match series 2-0, and both wins came on pitches that suited the fast bowlers. The first two ODIs were played at the same venues as the T20Is, and on the same strips, and they produced a very different type of cricket. New Zealand were sent in twice and were unable to bat out 41 overs on either occasion, as the ball moved off the seam and the bounce was steep and at times uneven. At Seddon Park, head groundsman Karl Johnson is working through a difficult build-up. A tractor-mounted machine called a verti-drain has been rumbling over the outfield, punching holes into the grass with its tines so that the ground gets more air and drains faster if the rain returns, as more rain is expected on Monday and Tuesday. The early expectation is for a more balanced surface than the ones seen in Auckland and Wellington, although the weather could still keep the seamers interested. MORE: List of teams who have lost an ODI series after taking 2-0 lead Seddon Park groundsman Karl Johnson on pitch preparation for IND vs NZ 3rd ODI According to Johnson, an unusually wet start to November across New Zealand is probably the biggest reason why the pitches have behaved the way they have this series. The T20Is before the ODIs were high-scoring affairs, with New Zealand making a record 259 at Eden Park and India chasing 199 in only 13.2 overs at Hnry Stadium in Wellington. The ODIs, in contrast, were low-scoring and dominated by the bowlers. He said the aim is to prepare a surface that stays consistent for 100 overs with minimal seam movement, but the unsettled conditions have made that harder. “New Zealand’s been pretty wet over the last few days, and we’ve had quite a lot of rain here yesterday, so we’ve lost out some time but we’ve been able to get the pitch ready,” he said in an interview wth Cricinfo. item.title: Utah Mammoth Ran Out of Gas Against Senators, and Goaltending Concerns Are Growing
item.description: The Utah Mammoth finally hit the wall. After five games on the road and three straight tests against quality opponents, fatigue caught up with them Saturday night in Ottawa. Utah opened the stretch with an impressive 3-2 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday before falling 5-4 in overtime to the Montreal Canadiens on Thursday. Against the Senators, the Mammoth controlled much of the game, outshooting Ottawa 32-21 and keeping pace for nearly 58 minutes. But the legs eventually gave out, and a couple of costly defensive lapses turned a competitive night into a 4-2 loss. Ottawa took advantage when Utah needed just two more minutes to secure at least a point. Nick Cousins found room around Barrett Hayton and MacKenzie Weegar, redirecting the puck past Karel Vejmelka for the late winner. It's a frustrating way to end a road trip, especially after Utah collected five points in five games. But the bigger concern coming out of Ottawa might be in the crease. It's Time to Give Sebastian Cossa the Net Karel Vejmelka was better Saturday. That doesn't necessarily mean he was good enough. The Utah goaltender stopped 17 of 20 shots, finishing with an .850 save percentage. Some of the damage came from defensive breakdowns, but Vejmelka also looked a step behind on several occasions. Whether it was getting across the crease or reacting to developing plays, he wasn't giving Utah the kind of goaltending it needs. At some point, the Mammoth have to stop treating this as a temporary slump. Vejmelka has now lost five of his last six starts, and Utah is no longer a rebuilding team that can afford to wait around for inconsistent goaltending. Sebastian Cossa deserves a legitimate opportunity to take over the starting job. The former Detroit Red Wings prospect arrived in Utah during the offseason, and the organization should find out what it has in him. There's also a bigger swing worth considering: Scott Wedgewood in Colorado. He's backing up Mackenzie Blackwood, but his recent track record suggests he can handle a starting workload. Last season, Wedgewood went 31-6-6 with a 2.02 goals-against average and a .921 save percentage. He's also entering the final year of his contract. If I'm Bill Armstrong, I'm at least picking up the phone and calling Colorado. Wedgewood could be a major upgrade, and Utah might be able to put together a deal that brings back draft capital while moving Vejmelka. The Mammoth are too good to keep gambling on goaltending.

item.title: Real Madrid legend Marcelo mocks Valencia defender after heated Mestalla encounter
item.description: Real Madrid legend Marcelo mocks Valencia defender after heated Mestalla encounter Real Madrid continued their impressive run of form with a convincing 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla . It was the eighth consecutive victory for Jose Mourinho’s side across all competitions, as Los Blancos head into the November international break in strong form. The encounter against Valencia was not without controversy, though, with defender Pablo Maffeo involved. The defender, who has a history of heated encounters with Los Blancos , once again found himself at the centre of attention. Marcelo takes aim at Maffeo This time, however, former Real Madrid superstar Marcelo could not resist taking a dig at the Spaniard on social media. “Maffeo really has it in for MADRID… my goodness,” Marcelo wrote on X , mockingly referring to the Valencia defender as ‘Masfeo’. “And a goal,” the Brazilian added, celebrating Madrid’s breakthrough during the first half. The incident came after Maffeo was penalised for a foul on Kylian Mbappe just outside Valencia’s penalty area. Maffeo received a yellow card for the challenge. Mbappe’s resulting free-kick struck the wall, and Fede Valverde collected the rebound to score Real Madrid’s opening goal. Maffeo was visibly frustrated with the decision and subsequently criticised the refereeing during his half-time interview with DAZN. “I don’t feel like doing this interview at all. It’s rubbish,” he complained , before insisting that the foul leading to Madrid’s opening goal should never have been awarded. Maffeo’s history with Real Madrid Maffeo has been involved in a series of controversies against Real Madrid, dating back to his time at Mallorca. At his former club, he was often involved in heated exchanges with Vinicius Jr., including controversial challenges and gestures towards the Brazilian. Pablo Maffeo’s personal vendetta against Real Madrid are well documented. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Although Maffeo previously claimed the pair had resolved their differences, it looks like he has now found a new bone to pick with Real Madrid. The important thing for Mourinho’s men was that they had the last laugh on Saturday and secured all three points. Maffeo is likely to receive a hostile reception when he visits the Santiago Bernabeu , and it remains to be seen how this battle pans out in future meetings.

item.title: Australia reach World Cup final after Fiji scare
item.description: Abbi Church (left) scored a hat-trick against Fiji - she now has seven tries in four 2026 World Cup matches [Getty Images] Australia (8) 30 Tries: Church 4, Upton, Chapman Goals: Kelleher 3 Fiji (8) 14 Tries: Yaranamua, Paseka Goals: Yaranamua 3 Australia have reached their fifth successive Women's Rugby League World Cup final as they seek a fourth consecutive title - but they were made to work harder than anyone expected. They had breezed through the group stages and there looked to be little to stop the procession. But World Cup debutants Fiji had other ideas. For 40 minutes, one of the biggest surprises in the history of rugby league looked eminently possible. Order was eventually restored, thanks largely to four tries from Abbi Church, which set Australia on their way to a 30-14 victory. They will face old rivals New Zealand in the final next Sunday in Brisbane, kicking off at 05:10 GMT. But having given New Zealand a scare in their opening match before losing 18-12, Fiji came out at Sydney Football Stadium fully intent to unsettle and confront the red-hot tournament favourites. In doing so, they became the first side since New Zealand in the 2013 World Cup final to open the scoring in a game against Australia, who trailed for the first time at this tournament. The tournament debutants put pressure on the Australia line from the start. Soon the entire Aussie team caught the bug with simple drops and brainless errors, and after 12 minutes Simaima Taufa conceded a penalty under the posts. Fiji opted to kick for two points. Four minutes later, they went all the way. Captain Sereana Naitokatoka stole the ball from Jaime Chapman 10 metres from the Australia line, and they drove through the defence for half-back Luisa Yaranamua to score. She also converted to give Fiji an astonishing 8-0 lead. At last Australia sparked into life, and two tries in the final 10 minutes of the opening half brought them level. Church drove over in the right corner, before Tamika Upton slipped through the defence as Australia returned pressure following a Fiji drop-out. But Jocelyn Kelleher missed twice from the tee to allow Fiji in at half-time level. Had Upton not brilliantly tipped a Fiji grubber behind, Australia would have trailed. Whatever coach Jess Skinner said in the changing room woke Australia up, and they took control. Church completed her treble - the third a brilliant catch from a booming Tarryn Aiken kick to the corner and before grounding the ball at full tilt - either side of Chapman diving over. Normal service resumed. But at last, the Jillaroos have been proved fallible - with a late Maria Paseka try providing a deserved flourish for fearless Fiji. Church, though, had the last word for Australia - collecting Losana Lutu's kick around 30 metres from her own line before racing clear to score.

item.title: Michael Carrick, Sir Alex Ferguson and Man United’s seemingly impossible question
item.description: Even as he risks being consigned to Manchester United history, Michael Carrick was talking about Manchester United’s history. They are celebrating one of their managers and, whether or not Aston Villa are defeated on Sunday, it is not him. Friday marked the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson ’s appointment. There is a dinner this weekend to honour the great Scot. There is also the chance Sunday marks Carrick’s last game at the helm. Ferguson has been in charge for two-thirds of the last four decades and end his tenure of his own volition, retiring after 26-and-a-half years. Carrick could become the seventh man sacked since then , without even including the interim appointment Ralf Rangnick. He is already the fifth of Ferguson’s former players to have served as caretaker manager. Ferguson has been the inspiration for them all. He remains the benchmark, the gold standard, but also the anomaly. A banner at Old Trafford, commemorating Ferguson, reads: “The impossible dream”. For much of the last 13 years, following him has seemed similarly impossible. “Well, it's not impossible,” Carrick countered. “Anything's possible. You've got to build, you've got to be realistic. You've got to put things in perspective as well, the recent history that we've had and where we want to get to, but it's not going to happen in a blink of an eye. It's not going to happen overnight. Success does take time, and we don't like having to spend time, but it does take a period of time to build.” That is true. That said, the inconvenient details are that it seemed to happen overnight when Carrick had an immediate impact upon his return to Old Trafford in January and that results show regression this season. United enter the weekend in 17th place in the Premier League , in a 14th consecutive campaign without a title challenge. In all competitions, they have a lone win in their last 10 matches. Matheus Cunha’s dramatic decider against Roma on Tuesday prompted suggestions it was Carrick’s Mark Robins moment ; there is a parallel of sorts because, a couple of weeks after Robins scored against Nottingham Forest in January 1990, Ferguson’s United were 17th. Then he was more than three years into his reign. Now Carrick is only three months into his first season after being appointed. If several of his predecessors think there was a brutality to their sacking, others can feel the United powerbrokers afforded them too much time. But the broader trend is that managers tend to be afforded less time now. “The game's certainly changed, no doubt,” Carrick reflected. “It always does. It evolved, and it had evolved to the stage probably after Sir Matt [Busby] in the years after that, to then Sir Alex.” Sir Alex Ferguson and Sir Matt Busby remain the only managers to have brought sustained success to Manchester United (PA Archive) The mention of Busby underlines the heights United have touched under two great empire-builders of managers, but rarely under anyone else. item.description: Dan Graziano of ESPN shared that he thinks the New England Patriots could move backup QB Tommy DeVito at the Trade Deadline. Getty The NFL Trade Deadline is rapidly approaching on Tuesday, November 10th. Most fans think first and foremost about adding players at the deadline. However, there have also been rumors that the Patriots could potentially move on from several players. The conversation about moving on from Patriots players has largely focused on the defensive side of the ball. Still, the opportunity to move players goes beyond that. Dan Graziano of ESPN even recently shared that the focus could be on quarterback Tommy DeVito. Could the New England Patriots Move Tommy DeVito? item.title: Report: Money too good to turn down for Bayern Munich for January friendly vs. Ajax in Kenya
item.description: DORTMUND, GERMANY - OCTOBER 03: Matthijs de Ligt of Ajax Amsterdam and Serge Gnabry of Bayern Muenchen battle for the ball during the Group A match of the UEFA Champions League between Borussia Dortmund and AS Monaco at Signal Iduna Park on October 3, 2018 in Dortmund, Germany. (Photo by TF-Images/TF-Images via Getty Images) | Getty Images The presence of a winter break in German football gives Bundesliga players a chance to spend around a week and a half with their families and recuperate while multiple other leagues play through Christmas and beyond. When the players return from their vacation, however, regaining match fitness is crucial ahead of the league’s restart. Given the relatively short timeframe, Bayern Munich has always preferred to limit themselves to just one friendly and keep it close to home, as evidenced by multiple recent January friendlies against RB Salzburg. This season, however, the plan is different. Bayern will travel to Nairobi, Kenya, to play a friendly against Ajax Amsterdam.According to reporter Manuel Bonke, (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) the friendly was not scheduled for the sake of preparing for the upcoming Bundesliga restart, but because the money was simply too good to turn down: Bayern will receive €5m for the trip to Nairobi, Kenya to play a friendly against Ajax on January 5th. Vincent Kompany approved the trip, which was then handled by Marketing and sales director Rouven Kasper. ‘For that kind of money, you have to do it’, it was said at Säbener Straße. It certainly is an unprecedented amount of money, though it is worth wondering how it will affect the Bavarians’ return to the Bundesliga season. They will face Borussia Mönchengladbach on January 9th, meaning the players will need to fly all the way back to Munich and get just over three days to rest before their next match. Will this be the only friendly of the winter pre- season camp? These are not insurmountable issues, and it is good that Kompany had the option to veto the trip. Furthermore, it should be nice for the fans in Kenya to see Bayern play Ajax. On a side note, it has also been far too long since Bayern has faced Ajax, but one can wonde r how such a trip will affect Bayern’s season restart. It worries me because… if they stayed here with me and my staff, we would give them very special attention when it comes to… to helping those players recover. But they’re going away with their national teams. And with the national teams… I can imagine, although I’ve never coached a national team, that their coaches want to work. item.description: Wyoming Cowboys tight end Kyle Frendt (83) catches the ball in the endzone during a college football game against the UNLV Rebels on Saturday, November 7, 2026, at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada. UNLV was down 41-21 when Dan Mullen decided to change quarterbacks. Exit Jackson Arnold. Enter Alex Orji. And the Michigan transfer nearly rallied the Rebels all the way back. item.title: Bernardo Silva hails Real Madrid dominance as red-hot Blancos extend winning streak with Valencia demolition
item.description: FBL-ESP-LIGA-VALENCIA-REAL MADRID - AFP Bernardo Silva has praised Real Madrid's defensive solidity after a commanding 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla. The Portuguese star believes their eighth consecutive win puts the club in a prime position to challenge for both Liga and Champions League glory this season. Real Madrid secure impressive victory Silva played a starring role as Madrid cruised to a 3-0 victory against Valencia at Mestalla. The Portuguese midfielder featured for 84 minutes during an excellent individual display in the heart of the pitch. The impressive away result marked an eighth consecutive win across all competitions for the Spanish club. Jose Mourinho’s side currently sits in second place in the Liga standings with 30 points - level with league leaders Barcelona, ​​who are set to play their 12th match of the campaign against Atletico Madrid. Silva highlights aggressive Valencia approach The match was not without its challenges for the visiting side. Silva noted the physical nature of their opponents and the lenient officiating that allowed the game to flow freely. "A tough match, in a challenging atmosphere, against an aggressive team and a referee who allowed them to be aggressive," Silva explained on the club's official website . "That made it complicated for us. Fede's [Valverde] stunning goal helped us control the game. I felt we always had control of the match and were very organized, managing their transitions very well. The defenders were very aggressive and won quick balls. We're very happy to secure three more points. "Having eight consecutive wins puts us in a much better position to fight for La Liga and be among the top eight in the Champions League. We're very happy with this streak, but now we need to focus on the next match and keep going because the atmosphere in the dressing room and at the club is very good. We want to keep winning and winning." Maintaining the winning streak Los Blancos have now recorded eight consecutive victories across all competitions. The last time they failed to secure a win was during the Madrid Derby against Atletico in late September. Silva emphasized that this achievement is crucial for his team if they wish to remain in contention for the title this season. "It's very important because the teams that defend best are always ready to win matches and titles," he added. "That puts us closer to winning games and championships." International duty calls for Silva Club football now pauses for the international break. Silva will immediately shift his focus to international duty and travel to join his Portugal team-mates. Portugal are preparing for two important UEFA Nations League fixtures in the coming days. They will face Denmark on November 14 before concluding the international window against Wales on November 17.
